inicio.titulo: An MCP server for your service, tested and on the current revision
inicio.lead: Tools the agent calls, with confirmation when there are consequences, a token when it's remote, and an automated test at the end. All on the 2026-07-28 revision of MCP, with the official SDK (v2, 2.3.1), in a kit that runs on your machine at no cost and with no key.
inicio.capa_alt: An MCP server for your service: a laptop with a terminal and a small server with a cable plugged in, on a dark desk.

numeros.t: official SDK version in the kit

inicio.aulas_sub: Each lesson ends with a command you run and an output you can check. The kit lives in the course's own repository.

itens: Devs who run Node and a terminal and want their service to be used by agents (Claude Code, Codex, and other MCP clients).
Anyone with an MCP server built in 2025 with SSE, session, and initialize who needs to know what changed.
If you prefer Python: the concepts apply equally; the course uses Node (the Python SDK mcp 2.3.0 contains server/discover in its code, with no hands-on practice here).
A server with a read-only tool, a tool with consequences, a resource, and a prompt.
The same code over stdio and over stateless Streamable HTTP, with a Host and Origin guard.
User confirmation mid-call (MRTR) and a token with minimum scope per tool.
An MCP Apps interface, the test suite, and the server hooked up to Claude Code and Codex.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in the WebMCP Track
itens: Course 0 shows how agents use a site; this one is the server side (backend).
Course 2 brings tools into the page with WebMCP; course 4 goes deeper into threats.
Autonomous-loop threats and in-depth evals belong to the LOOP-R Engenharia Track.
